void.purpose: The page ground; body, nav scrim, scrollbar track, nested rows.

surface.purpose: Cards, panels, small controls; first brightness step above void.

surface-hover.purpose: Hover fill for cards, ghost buttons and small controls.

hairline.purpose: 1px stroke on inputs and small controls only.

dust.purpose: Secondary text and icons; 7.04:1 on void.

dust-light.purpose: Placeholders, meta lines, small status copy; 9.66:1 on void.

ivory.purpose: Primary text and all headlines; 17.37:1 on void.

white.purpose: Top of the neutral ramp; rare true-white emphasis.

signal-amber.purpose: The only saturated colour: primary CTA, focus ring, caret, selection, active state.

signal-amber-deep.purpose: The amber fill one step down; primary button hover/press.

signal-amber-bright.purpose: The amber one step up; link hover.

success.purpose: A live, deployed or approved state — the Live pill dot, an approved gate, a passed deploy gate.

error.purpose: The error role — failed requests and error copy in every form, and the blocked status on the project page.

scrollbar-thumb.purpose: Browser scrollbar thumb on the void track.

display.purpose: Hero headline only — 48px base, 72px at 768px+, weight 700, -0.03em tracking, 1.05 line-height.

headline.purpose: Page and section titles — weight 600, 30px base (36px on the homepage section title), -0.03em/-0.02em tracking.

title.purpose: Card, panel and step headings — weight 500, 18px to 24px, -0.01em to -0.02em tracking.

body.purpose: Paragraph and form copy — weight 400, 16px, 1.625 line-height, max 65ch measure.

label.purpose: Field labels, buttons, nav links, inline controls — weight 500, 14px, -0.01em tracking. Micro-labels drop to 12px and 10px uppercase with positive tracking.

narrative.overview:
Skynet is a black room with the lights off and one amber signal burning in it. Everything else in the system — surfaces, borders, secondary type, icons — is a quiet graphite or off-white. That is the whole idea: a wide, dark, calm field in which a single saturated amber element is the only thing that asks to be touched. The palette was chosen so that the primary action can never be ambiguous, on any screen, at any brightness.

The register is professional and capable rather than swaggering. Skynet is for people who have never written code, so the system refuses the two things that would push them away: the category-default SaaS landing (centred headline over a row of equal feature cards) and the edgy developer-terminal look. Instead the type is a plain, well-set grotesque in two scales, the copy sits left-aligned in a single 1024px column, and the space is generous — the hero alone occupies the top half of the first viewport, and the process steps are set 56px apart.

Depth is tonal. A surface on the void is one brightness step up; the next step up is a hover state or a nested row; a row nested inside a card goes back down to the void. Nothing is outlined, and no card carries a drop shadow. The only ambient motion in the product is a three-depth field of drifting dust behind the hero, rendered entirely in CSS, which gives the black ground texture without ever competing with the content. The confirmed visual rejections are the category-default centred-hero-plus-equal-cards arrangement and the terminal/bitmap type register.
keyCharacteristics: One saturated accent in the whole system, spent on exactly one primary action per screen.
Depth by brightness step (void → surface → surface-hover) — surfaces are separated by tone, not by an outline or a raised edge.
One type family, two scales; hierarchy from size and weight contrast.
A three-depth drifting dust field as the only ambient motion, disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
Three radii only: 6px controls, 16px cards, full-round pills.
Browser surfaces (focus ring, caret, selection, scrollbar) themed from the same palette.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal amber is the only saturated hue in the system and it is spent once per screen — on the single primary action. Success, warning and error appear only as state markers. Rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Brightness-Step Rule
rules.body: A surface separates from the ground by being brighter, never by being outlined: void (#0A0A0A) → surface (#141414) → surface-hover (#1F1F1F). A row nested inside a card goes back down to void.

rules.name: The Hairline-Is-A-Control Rule
rules.body: The 1px hairline belongs to inputs and small controls. A card is defined by its fill and its radius; its edge is never drawn.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: One family — Archivo — at two scales. Hierarchy comes from size and weight contrast (700/600 against 500/400), never from a second typeface.

rules.name: The Tight-Upper Rule
rules.body: Every size above 20px is set tight: -0.03em at display, -0.02em at headline, -0.01em at title. Tracking loosens only as the size drops, and turns positive only on uppercase micro-labels.

rules.name: The Single-Column Rule
rules.body: Every surface is one centred column of at most 1024px (64rem) with 16px gutters. The column may contain a grid; the page never runs edge to edge — even the nav's inner content uses the same 1024px measure. The login surface narrows the same rule to 448px (28rem).

rules.name: The Ambient-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow in this system always means "this is emitting light" or "this is floating above scrolled content". There is no third job for a shadow, and brightness steps do the work that shadows do everywhere else.

rules.name: The Three Radii Rule
rules.body: A new element picks one of 6px, 16px, or full-round, and a component family never mixes them. Controls are the tightest thing on screen; containers are the softest.

dos: Do spend the amber signal once per screen on the single primary action, and let every other action be a ghost button or a quiet link.
Do separate a surface from the ground with one brightness step — surface, then surface-hover — rather than with an outline.
Do keep body copy to roughly 65 characters per line, left-aligned, and set anything above 20px tight.
Do give every interactive element the global focus treatment: a 2px amber ring with a 2px void offset.
Do pick from the three radii only — 6px controls, 16px cards, full-round pills — and keep a component family on one radius.
Do keep icons from lucide-react at a single stroke weight — 16px in most places, 14px in the wordmark, 12px on the project page's small action icons.
Do place the dust field behind content, never over it, and switch it off under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
donts: Don't introduce a second saturated accent; success, warning and error are states, and signal amber stays the one accent.
Don't put a border on a card, or reach for a shadow to separate a card from its neighbour — a brightness step does that.
Don't place more than one filled amber element in a viewport.
Don't mix radii inside one component family, and don't use a radius outside 6px, 16px or full-round.
Don't widen body copy past ~65ch or centre it; the system's voice is left-aligned inside the column.
Don't drop the focus ring, the amber caret, or the amber-on-void selection treatment — the browser surface is part of the system.
